requirements.title: Finalization selects a matching own final or a qualified fallback
requirements.source: 7.5.6.2, p1.finalizable-only, p1.exact-kind-rank-selection, p1.elemental-fallback, p1.assumed-rank-fallback, p1.no-selected-procedure; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102-103.
requirements.definition: For a finalizable entity, first select an own final of its dynamic type whose dummy has equal KIND parameter values and rank. Otherwise select a same-KIND elemental final or a same-KIND assumed-rank final. If neither condition applies, no procedure is called at this step. This does not omit the subsequent component or parent steps.

requirements.oracle:
Use distinct finalizer counters and defined primitive tokens. Compare callback kind/rank identity and counts rather than addresses. Use separate ordinary saved integer logs/counters, not reads of other objects already finalized. Initialize payloads through primitive named components rather than unintended whole-object assignments that themselves finalize the old left side. Keep every callback argument and accessed component defined. Pointer association and allocation inquiries require independently established valid states. Counter/order observers are IMPURE where side effects require it; do not silently place an impure finalizer behind a PURE function or procedure.

Finite process implementation: 7 run-phase cases represent 7 finite facets with mandatory guarded whole-allocatable DEALLOCATE events before observations. Exact log multisets and required partial-order edges are checked without peeking at finalized peers. 1 source/use graph facets remain pending. Source/case/evidence adjudications are separate content-bound records; authorship and observations do not confer approval.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not construct an illegal assumed-rank/exact-rank competition. Ordinary scalar finals are not elemental fallbacks, and finalizability alone is not a guarantee that this own-procedure step calls anything.

requirements.title: Declared nonallocatable finalizable components are finalized separately
requirements.source: 7.5.6.2, p1.nonallocatable-finalizable-components, p1.components-in-type-definition, p1.component-order-choice, p1.array-components-per-element; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102-103.
requirements.definition: After the own-procedure step, finalize the nonallocatable finalizable components appearing in the type definition. Their order is processor dependent. For an array entity, finalize each such component of each element separately, not one synthetic whole component array.

requirements.title: Own processing, declared components and finalizable parent processing are ordered stages
requirements.source: 7.5.6.2, p1.ordered-steps, p1.extended-type-condition, p1.finalizable-parent-condition, p1.parent-last; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102-103.
requirements.definition: Finalization follows the specified step sequence: own selected final, declared nonallocatable finalizable components, then the parent component when the entity is extended and the parent type is finalizable. The parent step invokes its own complete finalization process. Final subroutines are not inherited into the earlier own-selection step.

requirements.title: Finalizers must not access other event entities already finalized
requirements.source: 7.5.6.2, p2.multiple-entity-event, p2.no-reference-to-finalized-other, p2.no-definition-of-finalized-other; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 102-103.
requirements.definition: When an event finalizes several entities, their ordering is processor dependent. A final subroutine for one entity must not reference or define another of those entities after that other entity has been finalized. An assumed declaration or deallocation-list order cannot justify such access.
